ghs.en: She has a hairstyle similar to that of those three female magicians in that fantasy series that's super famous worldwide.

rows.en: She could not do magic, but she was known as a wizard with words.

ghs.en: She might not be able to use magic, but one could call her a sorceress of words.

rows.en: Once she started talking, she could not stop, and stopping her from starting was equally difficult.

ghs.en: It's impossible to stop her once she starts talking, and it's difficult to even stop her from wanting to talk.

rows.jp: 小娘の分際で語彙(ごい)も豊富なので、話していて飽きない。
rows.en: For a little brat, she had quite a vocabulary, so talking with her was never dull.

ghs.en: Her social class is rich in young femaleness, and her vocabulary is similarly rich, so one never grows tired of talking to her.
ghs.assessment: 小娘の分際で is a disparaging concessive, roughly 'for a little girl like her,' not a statement that her social class is rich in femininity. The English replaces the contrast between youth and vocabulary with a nonsensical social classification.
ghs.remedy: Use 'For a little girl, she has a rich vocabulary, so talking to her never gets boring.'

highlights.text: Her social class is rich in young femaleness

ghs.assessment: つるんでいる says that Miki often hangs out or associates with Kiri. 'Mate-ing' adds an animal or sexual implication, while the explanatory gloss of Kiri's name is absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miki often hangs out with the club's other first-year member, Sakura Kiri.'

rows.jp: ３０代の頃は泣く子を殺すと言われるほどに悪顔だった氏だが、ご両親の死後しばらくを経て、険の取れた豊かな顔つきへと変わっていった。
rows.en: In his thirties, Tazaki had a face said not merely to silence crying children, but to kill them. In the years after his parents died, however, the hard edges softened into the broad, benevolent face he wore today.

ghs.en: When he was in his thirties, he had the kind of nastiness in his face that is often used to scare crybabies to sleep ("kids who sleep grow up well, kids who cry die"), but sometime after the death of his parents, his face changed into one of abundance, its harshness lost.
ghs.assessment: The source hyperbolically says his face was so villainous that people said it could kill a crying child. The English changes killing into frightening children to sleep and inserts an unrelated explanatory proverb, materially rewriting the image.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In his thirties, he looked so menacing people said his face could kill a crying child.'

rows.jp: 遺産以外の何が、元暴走族の粗暴な鉄オタを善人に変えうるというのか。

ghs.assessment: The source asks rhetorically what other than an inheritance could have turned a rough former biker-gang member and railway obsessive into a good person. The English instead asserts that something outside the inheritance did so, loses 'former,' and converts two traits into a comparison between them.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What besides an inheritance could turn a rough former biker and train fanatic into a good man?'

ghs.en: Taichi: "You really manage to wear that hot-looking thing often, can't you."
ghs.assessment: Here よく expresses amazement at how she can bear such warm-looking clothing, not frequency. The English inserts 'often' and leaves 'hot-looking' open to a different sense instead of describing an outfit that looks stifling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How can you stand wearing something that looks so hot?'

ghs.en: Touko: "..."

rows.jp: 無視。
rows.en: Ignored.

ghs.en: Ignored.

rows.jp: 「へいへい」
rows.en: ‘Yeah, yeah.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hey hey."
ghs.assessment: へいへい is a resigned or dismissive 'yeah, yeah' or 'all right, all right.' Rendering it as the attention-getting greeting 'hey hey' changes the speech act.

rows.jp: 肩をすくめて、冬子のすぐ隣……自分の席に座る。
rows.en: I shrugged and dropped into my own seat—right next to Touko.

ghs.en: Shrugging my shoulder, I sit in the seat next Touko's... mine.

rows.jp: まるでハリネズミだ。
rows.en: She was a hedgehog.

ghs.en: Just like a hedgehog.

rows.jp: 最近は、針に磨きがかかっている。
rows.en: Lately, she had been honing her quills.

ghs.en: And lately, taken to polishing those needles.
ghs.assessment: 針に磨きがかかっている says the figurative quills have lately become even sharper or more formidable. The English invents an omitted subject actively taking up the habit of polishing them.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Lately, her quills have grown sharper still.'

rows.jp: 誰に対してもそうだから、気に病むこともない。
rows.en: She treated everyone that way, so there was no reason to take it personally.

ghs.en: It's the same with everyone, so it's nothing to be worried about.

rows.jp: けど俺に対しての針は……少し毒を含んでいる気がする。
rows.en: But the quills she turned on me... seemed to carry a trace of venom.

ghs.en: But the needles set against me... feel like they have a bit of poison in them.

rows.jp: 気のせいかもしれない。
rows.en: Maybe it was all in my head.

ghs.en: Maybe it's just my imagination, I don't know,

rows.jp: 自意識過剰なだけかも。
rows.en: Maybe I was just being self-conscious.

ghs.en: it might just be my excessive self-consciousness, perhaps,

rows.jp: けど。
rows.en: But.

ghs.en: but,

rows.jp: けれども。
rows.en: And yet.

ghs.en: and also however,

rows.jp: そう考えただけで。
rows.en: The thought alone was enough.

ghs.en: just by thinking that,

rows.jp: 発作は起こった。
rows.en: The episode struck.

ghs.en: I had a seizure.

rows.jp: 「いかんね。いかんいかん」
rows.en: ‘No. No, no.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cut it out now! Cut it out cut it out!"

rows.jp: 幸い発作は小さなもので、理性が消し飛ぶ危険はなかった。
rows.en: Fortunately, it was a mild one, with no danger of blowing my reason clean away.

ghs.en: Fortunately the fit was small, so there was no danger of it scattering my rationality.

rows.jp: 逆流した胃液を呑み込む悪寒と引き替えに、そいつの頭を奈落に押し込める。
rows.en: I forced its head back into the abyss, paying for it with a shudder as I swallowed the acid surging up my throat.

ghs.en: In exchange for the chills of swallowing acid reflux, its head is imprisoned back in the hellish abyss.

rows.jp: 異形の舌先が、ちろりと地表を薙(な)いだ。
rows.en: The tip of its misshapen tongue flicked across the surface.

ghs.en: The tip of its heteromorphic tongue is scythed down in a flash, and lays calm on the surface of the earth.
ghs.assessment: The source makes the tip of the grotesque tongue briefly flick or sweep across the surface. The English instead makes the tongue the passive object of being scythed down and adds that it comes to rest calmly, reversing agency and inventing a result.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The tip of its misshapen tongue flicked across the surface.'

highlights.text: The tip of its heteromorphic tongue is scythed down in a flash, and lays calm on the surface of the earth.

rows.jp: 「なあ」
rows.en: ‘Hey.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hey."

rows.en: ‘...What?’

ghs.en: Touko: "...what."

rows.jp: いい加減うんざりといった調子で、冬子。
rows.en: Touko answered, sounding thoroughly fed up.

ghs.en: A tone that sounds just about fed up with fooling around, Touko's.

rows.jp: 「お尻のとこ、破れてパンツ見えてる」
rows.en: ‘Your skirt's torn in back. I can see your panties.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Around your ass there's a tear, and I can see your panties."

rows.jp: 慌てて立ち上がり、両手で尻をまさぐる。
rows.en: She sprang up and frantically ran both hands over her butt.

ghs.en: Standing up in a panic, she gropes her behind with both hands.

rows.jp: 「なんつったりして」
rows.en: ‘Just kidding.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awww what a dumb thing I said."
ghs.assessment: なんつったりして is a playful retraction equivalent to 'just kidding' or 'or so I say.' The English turns it into remorseful self-criticism and fails to reveal the preceding claim as a prank.

highlights.text: Awww what a dumb thing I said.

rows.jp: ばちーん！！
rows.en: SMACK!!

ghs.en: Ker-smack!!!

rows.jp: 「ぐふっ」
rows.en: ‘Guh!’

ghs.en: Taichi: "G'fuh!"

rows.jp: 不意の平手うち。
rows.en: A slap out of nowhere.

ghs.en: Sudden palm strike.

rows.jp: スリップダウン。
rows.en: Down I went.

ghs.en: Bail into slipdown.
ghs.assessment: The source consists only of the stylized loan expression 'slip down.' Adding 'bail into' imports an unsupported racing or motorcycle maneuver rather than simply describing the fall.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Slip down.' or a functional 'Down I went.'

rows.jp: 見事に転ぶ。
rows.en: A magnificent fall.

ghs.en: A magnificent fall.

rows.jp: 「いててて」
rows.en: ‘Ow ow ow.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "OwChChCh!"

rows.jp: 冬子はもう、先刻と変わらぬ姿勢で座っていた。
rows.en: Touko had already resumed precisely the same pose as before.

ghs.en: Touko was already sitting in the exact unchanging posture as moments before.

rows.jp: 「冗談だってのに」
rows.en: ‘It was only a joke.’

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I was just kidding!"
Touko: "..."

rows.jp: 相手をしてくれるつもりはないらしい。
rows.en: Apparently, she had no intention of humoring me.

ghs.en: It doesn't look like she's looking to play around with someone.

rows.jp: 澄ましていて排他的で。
rows.en: Cool, collected, and shutting everyone out.

ghs.en: Clannishly demure.

rows.jp: でも意外と、心の隙は多い。
rows.en: Yet she let her guard down surprisingly often.

ghs.en: But hearts, surprisingly, have many openings.
ghs.assessment: The source remains about this particular person: despite her aloofness, she has surprisingly many openings in her emotional guard. The plural 'hearts' turns the observation into a generic claim and removes its subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But surprisingly, she leaves plenty of openings in her guard.'

rows.jp: 鞄を机に放って、冬子以外誰もいない教室を眺め渡す。
rows.en: I tossed my bag onto the desk and surveyed the classroom, empty except for Touko.

ghs.en: I dump my bag on the desk and pass a lost gaze on the classroom, empty with the exception of Touko.

rows.jp: まだ始業まで間がある。
rows.en: There was still some time before classes began.

ghs.en: There's still time before we begin.

rows.jp: どうしよう。
rows.en: What now?

ghs.en: What to do.

rows.jp: 屋上に行く
rows.en: Go to the roof

rows.jp: 冬子と話す
rows.en: Talk to Touko
